tier_reason: README table compares sliceslice 0.2.0 against Rust std 1.46.0 String::find (plus memmem, twoway, sse4-strstr) with the i386 Criterion benchmark that is public at tag v0.2.1 (benches/i386.rs, now bench/benches/i386.rs), Rust 1.46.0 and gcc 9.3.0 stated, build flags public in the tagged Cargo.toml and sse4-strstr/build.rs (default cargo bench profile, -std=c++11 -march=native for the C++ row), and CPU Intel Core i7-6700 stated.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust 1.46.0 and gcc 9.3.0 (README). The published table was produced by the v0.2.1-era harness (benches/i386.rs at tag v0.2.1, criterion 0.3, no [profile.bench] override, so cargo bench defaults at opt-level 3; the sse4-strstr C++ wrapper is compiled by sse4-strstr/build.rs with -std=c++11 -march=native). The current bench/ crate (criterion 0.5, [profile.bench] lto = true, codegen-units = 1) came later and was not used for the README numbers.
corrections.workload: Criterion 'i386' benchmark (benches/i386.rs at tag v0.2.1; now bench/benches/i386.rs): short haystack: words of data/words.txt sorted by length, each searched in every later word; long haystack: every word searched in data/i386.txt (read with fs::read and from_utf8_lossy at v0.2.1, include_bytes in the current bench); single-pattern substring search returning a bool. sliceslice and memmem searchers are constructed outside the timed loop; String::find, twoway and sse4-strstr build per call.
corrections.caveats: Baseline is Rust 1.46 std String::find (2020), not libc memmem or any C++ std; README numbers are for sliceslice 0.2.0 on 2020 toolchains with the v0.2.1 harness, and the README table omits the memchr::memmem rows the current bench now runs. The benchmark is asymmetric: sliceslice (and memmem) searchers are prebuilt outside the timed loop while String::find rebuilds its Two-Way searcher per call, so needle preprocessing is excluded only for the prebuilt rows. In BurntSushi's memchr rebar record (benchmarks/record/x86_64/2026-07-30.csv, sliceslice 0.4.3) sliceslice oneshot is about 2.17x faster than libc memmem by geomean of medians over 39 benchmarks (faster on 30) and about 3.9x faster than Rust std memmem oneshot (faster on 34 of 38), but prebuilt sliceslice beats memchr 2.8.3 prebuilt on only 15 of 42 benchmarks (geomean 0.90x) (derived from that CSV; older records 2023-12-29 and 2025-09-25 give 2.08x and 2.14x vs libc). Open issue #97 (January 2025, no maintainer reply) reports that Avx2Searcher can read past the end of the haystack (OOB read in vector_search_in_chunk); the API is unsafe and x86 AVX2 only; issue #47 recorded a performance regression with Rust 1.52.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly (335.56 vs 79.416 ms, 345.01 vs 35.181 ms; 4.2x and 9.8x derived). Record's flags described the current bench crate (criterion 0.5, LTO, codegen-units=1), which postdates the 2020 table; corrected to the v0.2.1 harness. Shortcomings: Rust-std baseline rather than libc/C++, prebuilt-vs-oneshot asymmetry, slower than memchr::memmem prebuilt on most rebar benchmarks, open OOB-read soundness issue #97; metadata (MIT, 106 stars, last commit 2024-09-20, stale) checked.

tier_reason: First-party README tables from Arm optimized-routines' public string/bench/memcpy.c compare __memcpy_a72 against the libc 'memcpy' row and Arm's __memcpy_aarch64/__memcpy_aarch64_simd, but no compiler, flags, board, SoC or clock are given (only 'cortex-a72'), so not A; no independent measurement found.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the benchmark. The library's Makefile builds the assembly with CPPFLAGS -fPIC -g -fno-inline -fno-builtin-inline -fno-inline-functions -fno-builtin and LDFLAGS -shared; compiler version unstated.
corrections.workload: Arm optimized-routines memcpy benchmark (string/bench/memcpy.c) on a Cortex-A72: random copies (16384 copies with lengths from a SPEC2017-derived size distribution under 4 KB) over 32K to 1024K working sets, aligned and unaligned medium copies 8 B to 512 B, large copies 1K to 64K, and forwards/backwards unaligned memmove 1K to 64K, in bytes per ns.
corrections.caveats: The repo's stated purpose is a device-memory fix (re-ordered stores in the 96-byte path for framebuffers/SPDK); the code is an initial import of Arm optimized-routines memcpy (Arm MIT header; memset.S is MIT OR Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception; COPYING is MIT, Solidrun Ltd 2021), loaded via LD_PRELOAD. README tables (added July 2022) give no compiler, flags, board, SoC or clock, and the code was reworked again in January 2024 after the numbers were published. The 'memcpy' row is the system libc (presumably glibc). Gains are mostly small aligned sizes (8-64 B: 1.36-1.75x over libc, 1.18-1.50x over __memcpy_aarch64); random and large copies are within 1-2%; the backwards-memmove 64K win (11.69 vs 6.54) is shared by Arm's __memcpy_aarch64 (11.67); unaligned 64 B (8.46 vs 9.35) and backwards memmove 1K-8K (e.g. 16.48 vs 16.70 at 4K) are slightly slower than libc.

notes: All quoted numbers appear in the README (derived ratios correct). Main shortcomings: unspecified hardware/compiler, numbers predate the January 2024 rework, gains confined to 8-64 B copies and largely inherited from Arm optimized-routines (an already-known incumbent), a few rows slower than glibc. License MIT confirmed (COPYING, Solidrun Ltd); 5 stars; last commit 2024-01-07 (stale); not a GitHub fork, but code lineage is ARM-software/optimized-routines.

tier_reason: First-party README gives one Keil timing (10000 bytes x 10000: rt_memcpy 1261 ms, assembly 883 ms, C library memcpy 906 ms) with no benchmark code, MCU, clock, compiler version or flags, so C.

corrections.caveats: The win over the Keil C library memcpy is about 2.6% (906 vs 883 ms) from one undocumented run; README gives no benchmark code, MCU, clock, Keil version or optimisation level; the large gain (1.43x) is against RT-Thread's own C rt_memcpy. The assembly is Silicon Labs uC/LIB code (Copyright 2004-2020 Silicon Laboratories, SPDX Apache-2.0 headers in all three ports, Keil/GCC/IAR), so the Apache-2.0 licence is consistent; memory buffers are not checked for overlap (memcpy semantics only). Last commit 2022-06-09.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly. Provenance concern in the record is resolved: every .S file carries Silicon Labs and RT-Thread SPDX Apache-2.0 headers, so usability is copyable, not mixed. Split id: merged.json also holds https://github.com/mysterywolf/rt_memcpy_cm (category hand-written-asm-kernels, verify batch-33); record one of the two as duplicate. Shortcomings: ~3% win over C library, single unspecified Keil run, abandoned (12 stars).
